title: ⭐ Practice: the words of the laboratory

questions.prompt: A hospital checks the genetic material of a man who feels perfectly well, in order to find out whether he is likely to develop a disease later in life. Which term of the module names that check?

options.text: gene therapy
genetic testing
blood clotting
germline gene therapy

questions.explanation: genetic testing is defined in your book as the checking of an individual's genetic material to predict present or future disability or disease, which is word for word what the hospital is doing. gene therapy is the insertion of normal DNA directly into cells to correct a defect, so it treats a disease instead of looking for one. germline gene therapy inserts genes into embryos so that the change is passed on to later generations, and it is a treatment too, aimed at children who do not yet exist. blood clotting is the process in which liquid blood changes into a semisolid and has nothing to do with reading anybody's genes.

questions.prompt: Your module ends its listening work with a list of pairs of opposites. Which word is the opposite of "conceal"?

options.text: hide
deny
show
reduce

questions.explanation: The module pairs conceal with "show": to conceal is to keep something out of sight, and to show is to put it in plain view. "hide" is the trap, because it means very nearly the same as conceal, so it is a synonym and never an opposite. "deny" belongs to another pair of the same list, the one it forms with confess. "reduce" belongs to the pair it forms with enhance, which is about size and quality rather than about what is visible.

questions.prompt: A laboratory report states that a technician "misread the label". What does the prefix add to the verb?

options.text: It says the technician read the label wrongly.
It says the technician did not read the label.
It says the technician read the label again.
It says the technician read the label out loud.

questions.explanation: mis- is not a plain negation: it says the action was carried out wrongly or badly, so the technician did read the label and got it wrong, exactly as misunderstand means understanding the wrong way. "It says the technician did not read the label." is what a true negative prefix would give, and mis- never does that; had he not read it at all, the report would say so plainly. "It says the technician read the label again." is the meaning of re-, another prefix altogether. "It says the technician read the label out loud." invents a meaning that no prefix in the module carries.

questions.prompt: A father tells his son: "You may take my mobile phone to the match, but you mustn't switch it off." Read the two modals. Which reading is right?

options.text: The first states a possibility; the second states that something is not possible.
The first forbids; the second gives permission.
Both give permission, the second one more firmly than the first.
The first gives permission; the second forbids.

questions.explanation: may is the modal of permission, so the son is allowed to take the phone; mustn't is the modal of prohibition, so switching it off is not allowed. "The first forbids; the second gives permission." swaps the two modals round and hands the son the opposite instructions. "Both give permission, the second one more firmly than the first." turns a ban into a second permission, which the negative form cannot possibly be. "The first states a possibility; the second states that something is not possible." is the reading that belongs to can and can't: a father who says mustn't is not describing what the world allows, he is laying down a rule.

questions.prompt: Rewrite this in three words, using a compound adjective: "a study that lasted five years".

options.text: a five-years study
a five-year study
a study five-year
a fifth-year study

questions.explanation: A number and a noun make one block in front of the noun they describe, and the noun inside that block stays singular, which gives "a five-year study", exactly as your book turns a period of six months into a six-month period. "a five-years study" keeps the plural -s inside the block, and the block never carries one. "a fifth-year study" replaces the number five with the ordinal fifth and so names the fifth year of something instead of a length of five years. "a study five-year" leaves the block behind its noun, and a compound adjective of this kind always stands in front of the noun it describes.

questions.prompt: One of the module's articles says a gene was taken from a strain of beans; another speaks of the deadly bird flu strain. Which statement about the word "strain" is right here?

options.text: A type of virus in both.
A variety of a plant in both.
A variety of a plant in the first, a type of virus in the second.
A physical effort in the first, a variety of a plant in the second.

questions.explanation: One word can carry several meanings, and the sentence around it decides which one you read: beans are a plant, so the first strain is a variety of plant, while bird flu is an illness carried by a virus, so the second strain is a type of virus. "A type of virus in both." would make the gene come from a virus, and the article says it was taken from beans. "A variety of a plant in both." would make bird flu a plant. "A physical effort in the first, a variety of a plant in the second." picks a third real meaning of strain, the effort you put on a muscle, which no article of this module uses, and then puts the plant on the wrong side.
